newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ex-Mercedes manager arrested in South of France.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Mercedes manager arrested in South of France.

text.p: A former executive of Mercedes-Benz AG accused of misappropriating millions of marks has been arrested on the French Riviera, German police said on Friday.
Fifty-five year-old Hans Dieter Fink was apprehended in a restaurant at Menton, a resort on the Cote d'Azur, on Thursday, the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) said in a statement.

Fink, a head of department in charge of car sales to Russia and other former Soviet Union states until May 1994, allegedly sold vehicles to car dealers at discounts in exchange for bribes, the Stuttgart public prosecutors' office said.

"He is accused of breach of trust to the disadvantage of the company and bribery," Gernot Blessing, a spokesman for the Stuttgart state prosecutors' office said. Police said he allegedly caused Mercedes 10 million marks worth of damage.
Blessing said Fink was still in French police custody and that Germany would issue an extradition request. But extradition could be delayed if Fink contested it, he added.
There had been a warrant out for Fink's arrest since last year. Police said he had been on the run since May 1995 but had kept in touch with his family and friends.
